Does a VWFA signal spike, confirmed by Wernicke's area 100–150 ms later, mark the moment a word is read?

Five example sentences, run end-to-end through the detector: pipeline/word_detection.py classifies VWFA-ROI amplitude into low / medium-high / very-high bands, requires a corroborating rise in the Wernicke ROI shortly after, then drops a 400 ms marker (±200 ms) on the confirmed point — compared here against the real fixation-derived word timing.

How a marker gets placed

1 · Envelope

Band-pass + Hilbert envelope of the VWFA-ROI average (E50, E58, E64, E69), smoothed over 60 ms.

2 · Classify

Data-calibrated percentiles split the envelope into low / medium-high / very-high — never a fixed µV cutoff.

3 · Candidate

Sustained medium-high runs (≥40 ms) peak-pick a candidate; a 250 ms refractory period stops one word firing twice.

4 · Confirm

Wernicke ROI (E34, E39, E40) must also rise, 100–150 ms after the VWFA peak.

5 · Mark

Confirmed point gets a 400 ms window: 200 ms before, 200 ms after.

Read this honestly

01

The three-level VWFA hypothesis is untested, not proven. This run shows detected events landing near real word boundaries more often than not — that's evidence worth pursuing, not confirmation of the underlying neuroscience.

02

Thresholds are calibrated on 5 sentences with no true resting/no-word baseline. "Low" here means low relative to these 122 words, not a validated absolute floor. The baseline_vs_reading calibration mode is ready for when the full continuous ZuCo recording is available.

03

The 105-channel order in eeg.npy is an unverified assumption — 104 ascending E-numbered channels plus Cz, since the source .mat with true channel locations isn't present on this machine.
